node-1.label: A woman in her 60s presented with worsening dyspnea on exertion and pedal edema developing gradually over 2 months

node-2.label: She had no medical history and was only taking over-the-counter vitamin supplements; she was at her baseline functional status until 2 months ago when symptoms began progressing

node-3.label: Physical examination showed heart rate 125 beats/min, blood pressure 100/70 mm Hg, jugular venous distention, and bilateral pedal edema

why.why: Echocardiogram shows severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction (EF 15-20%) with grade 2 diastolic dysfunction, and BNP is markedly elevated at 1700 pg/mL. Both laboratory and radiology expert analyses interpret these as definitive confirmation of heart failure/volume overload. These objective findings, combined with the gradual dyspnea, tachycardia, JVD, and pedal edema, strongly confirm the diagnosis, raising confidence from 0.65 to 0.95.

Echocardiography reveals severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction (EF 15-20%) and BNP is markedly elevated at 1700 pg/mL. Both laboratory and radiology expert analyses state these findings definitively refute primary pulmonary hypertension as the underlying cause and indicate that any pulmonary hypertension is secondary to left heart failure. Therefore primary pulmonary hypertension syndrome is highly unlikely, and confidence is lowered from 0.05 to 0.02.

There is no renal history, and echocardiography shows severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction that explains the fluid overload and edema. Both laboratory and radiology expert analyses interpret the markedly elevated BNP and echo findings as refuting primary renal disease as the underlying cause, so confidence is lowered from 0.05 to 0.02.

node-8.label: BNP is markedly elevated at 1700 pg/mL

node-9.label: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF)

why.why: Echocardiography shows severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction (EF 15-20%) with grade 2 diastolic dysfunction, and BNP is markedly elevated at 1700 pg/mL. Laboratory and radiology expert analyses explicitly state these objective findings definitively confirm HFrEF and recommend clinical management for HFrEF. This fully accounts for the dyspnea on exertion, tachycardia, JVD, and pedal edema, raising confidence from 0.90 to 0.95.

node-10.label: Pulmonary hypertension is secondary to left heart failure

attrs.why: Severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction (EF 15-20%) and markedly elevated BNP indicate left heart failure as the cause of any pulmonary hypertension. Expert analyses explicitly note that any pulmonary hypertension is secondary to left heart failure rather than primary, so this is highly likely.
